node_definition.done_when: reckon.crew.repair decides an absent severity by the review record's own timestamp field against a module constant naming when stored reviews began to be refused for unmarked findings (2026-10-01T07:14:36+00:00, the landing of the write-time severity audit, with a comment naming that mechanism, not a plan or ticket). A finding with no severity on a record stamped before it stays blocking, as today. One on a record stamped at or after it is not repaired, and is reported as unmarked: the composed node, or the no-repair result, lists the unmarked findings by file and line. dispatch_repair_for_run's recorded reason for a round that composes no repair names the unmarked count beside the follow-on count. A new tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_reported_not_repaired.py covers: an old unmarked record repaired; a new unmarked-only record composing no repair, with a reason naming the unmarked count; a new record mixing one blocking and one unmarked finding, repairing only the blocking one and listing the unmarked one. tests/test_repair_answers_only_blocking_findings.py still passes. Only the named test files are run, with no call reaching SLURM and no real worker launched, each log ending with an EXIT= line; the coordinator runs the wider population at merge. Before status complete, delete every directory you created under /tmp, print what you delete, and list it in artifacts.
